_about: Buildings and features a DM can add to a place from its page: temples (sized by the settlement, with services and prices), and features a town might be built around (decorative, defensive, important or historical). {name} is the place.

services.name: Release from an unjust oath or contract
A blessing for a new building or field
Sanctioned demolition, with the land's spirits appeased
Registration of a contract of service
A disguise for a festival, or a new name for a fresh start
A blessing for a boat or a voyage
Training in arms, for the faithful
Hosting of a feast or celebration
Weather-reading and a blessing against storms
Cleansing of a home after a death or curse
Sanctuary for a fugitive, for three days
A funeral pyre, and a song for the dead

details: Its doors are never locked.
Its bells ring the hours for the whole town.
Its walls are covered in offerings and prayers.
It is far grander than the town around it.
It is half ruined, and the priest is rebuilding it alone.
It doubles as the town's school.
Pilgrims sleep in its yard.
Its altar stone is older than the building.
Its roof is gilded, paid for by one rich family who make sure everyone knows.
A great tree grows through the middle of it, and the priests say the god planted it.
Its walls are painted with scenes of the god's legends, faded and touched up in brighter colours.
It has a hospital wing where the sick sleep in rows.
Its crypt holds the bones of local heroes, and pilgrims come to touch them.
Its priest is a former adventurer whose old team still visits.
It runs the only school in the area, and the children sing at every service.
It's built from the stones of an older temple to a different god.
A holy spring rises in its courtyard.
Its bell was cast from melted-down weapons after a war.
A stray dog lives in the doorway and is said to be blessed.
It keeps a book where travellers write their names, going back centuries.
Its doors are carved with the names of every priest who has served there.
It feeds the poor every evening from a great kettle.
It's built on stilts above the floodwaters.
It has a library of prayers in a dozen languages.
Its incense is made from a local herb and can be smelled across the town.
secrets: The priest has lost their faith and goes through the motions.
The offerings box has been robbed for months.
A cult meets in the crypt on the dark moon.
The temple holds a relic another church wants back.
The priest is spying for the church's leaders in the city.
The temple's debts are owed to a dangerous house.
The holy relic on the altar is a fake; the real one was sold years ago.
The priest has a family the church doesn't know about.
The temple is hiding a fugitive from the law.
A demon is bound under the altar, and the wards are weakening.
The priest has been granting divine essences to people the god didn't choose.
The temple's spring is drying up, and the priest is faking its flow.
A noble pays the temple to keep a dangerous secret about his family.
The temple is a front for smuggling relics across the border.
The crypt connects to a forgotten astral space.
The priest is dying and hasn't named a successor.
Someone has been stealing from the poor box, and it's the acolyte everyone trusts.
The god's voice hasn't been heard here in a generation, and the priests are afraid to say so.
A cult of a rival god is slowly taking over the congregation.
The temple's founder made a pact with an astral power, not a god.

features.name: The painted walls
features.text: Every outer wall in {name} is painted with scenes from the town's history, repainted each spring.
features.dm: One panel was painted over in a hurry years ago. Under it is a scene someone wanted forgotten.

features.name: The glass bell tower
features.text: A slender tower of green glass rises over {name}, ringing softly whenever the wind turns.
features.dm: The glass was poured by an essence user who never asked for payment, and never left town.

features.name: The hanging gardens
features.text: Terraces of flowers and herbs spill down every wall around the square of {name}.
features.dm: The gardener feeds the plants something that makes them bloom out of season.

features.name: The mosaic square
features.text: The square of {name} is a mosaic of a great beast, laid in coloured stone.
features.dm: The beast was real. The mosaic shows where it is buried.

features.name: The lantern street
features.text: A street of {name} is hung with hundreds of paper lanterns, lit every night by the children.
features.dm: One lantern is never lit. Lighting it is a signal for smugglers.

features.name: The carved gate
features.text: The town gate of {name} is carved with the faces of every headman it has had.
features.dm: The newest face was carved before that headman took office.

features.name: The singing fountain
features.text: A fountain in {name} hums a low note when the water runs, and townsfolk tune their instruments by it.
features.dm: A small mana spring feeds it. The Magic Society would like to know.

features.name: The statue of the founder
features.text: A weathered statue of {name}'s founder looks out over the road.
features.dm: The founder was a bandit. The town tells another story.

features.name: The rooftop dovecotes
features.text: Every roof in {name} has a dovecote, and the doves carry messages for a copper.
features.dm: One flock flies to a place no one in town admits to knowing.

features.name: The festival arch
features.text: A great wooden arch, hung with ribbons from every festival, stands at the edge of {name}.
features.dm: The oldest ribbons are wards, tied there by someone who knew what they were doing.

features.name: The old palisade
features.text: A palisade of sharpened logs rings {name}, mended so often that hardly an old log is left.
features.dm: There is a gap behind the tannery that the watch pretends not to know about.

features.name: The stone keep
features.text: A squat stone keep stands in the middle of {name}, big enough for everyone to shelter in.
features.dm: The keep's cellar runs into older tunnels nobody has mapped.

features.name: The ward-stones
features.text: A ring of carved ward-stones around {name} keeps lesser monsters away.
features.dm: One stone has cracked, and the ward is weaker on that side than anyone knows.

features.name: The watchtowers
features.text: Three watchtowers on the hills around {name} light beacons when anything comes.
features.dm: One watchman sleeps on duty, and takes bribes to say he didn't.

features.name: The moat
features.text: {name} sits behind a broad moat fed by the river, crossed by a single drawbridge.
features.dm: Something lives in the moat. It has been fed for years.

features.name: The militia hall
features.text: The militia of {name} drills in a long hall hung with old weapons and trophies.
features.dm: Some trophies were bought, not won.

features.name: The bell of warning
features.text: A great bronze bell hangs at the centre of {name}; it has rung only three times in living memory.
features.dm: The last time it rang, nothing came. Nobody admits to ringing it.

features.name: The hidden refuge
features.text: In a crisis the folk of {name} hide in caves above the town, stocked with food and water.
features.dm: The caves were stocked recently. Someone knows a crisis is coming.

features.name: The thorn hedge
features.text: A hedge of iron-hard thorns, grown by some old essence user, surrounds {name}.
features.dm: The hedge grows a little closer every year.

features.name: The river chain
features.text: A great chain can be raised across the river at {name} to stop boats.
features.dm: Whoever holds the winch key holds the river. The key is missing.

features.name: The great well
features.text: {name} was built around a deep well that never runs dry, even in drought.
features.dm: The well is far deeper than any well should be, and something down there is breathing.

features.name: The crossroads stone
features.text: {name} grew up around a stone where four roads meet; travellers touch it for luck.
features.dm: The stone is a waymarker from before the current age, and it points somewhere.

features.name: The ford
features.text: {name} sits at the only safe ford for miles, and lives off the travellers who cross.
features.dm: A rival village upstream has been talking about building a bridge.

features.name: The mill race
features.text: A long mill race brings water from the hills to the wheels of {name}.
features.dm: Whoever controls the sluice gate upstream could ruin the town in a day.

features.name: The market cross
features.text: Traders have met at the market cross of {name} for longer than the town has stood.
features.dm: The right to hold the market is written on a charter the council has lost.

features.name: The shrine spring
features.text: A spring sacred to the church rises in {name}, and pilgrims come to drink from it.
features.dm: The spring's healing is real but fading. The priests are keeping it quiet.

features.name: The old mine
features.text: The old mine above {name} made the town rich once; now it is mostly worked out.
features.dm: There is a vein no one has found yet. One miner knows where it is.

features.name: The harbour wall
features.text: A curved harbour wall shelters the boats of {name} from the worst of the weather.
features.dm: The wall is crumbling. A bad storm would take half the fleet.

features.name: The grain store
features.text: {name} keeps a great stone granary that can feed the town through two bad winters.
features.dm: Half the grain is gone. Someone has been selling it.

features.name: The astral door
features.text: An old, sealed astral space door stands on the edge of {name}; the Adventure Society checks it every month.
features.dm: The seal has been opened and closed again recently.

features.name: The teleportation circle
features.text: {name} has a small teleportation circle, run by the Church of the Journey and the Magic Society, and passage costs a fee in spirit coins.
features.dm: The circle's keeper lets some people through without the fee, for a price of another kind.

features.name: The Adventure Society post
features.text: A small Adventure Society post in {name} posts contracts and pays bounties on monster cores.
features.dm: The clerk is skimming from the bounties.

features.name: The battlefield
features.text: A battle was fought in the fields outside {name} long ago, and ploughs still turn up bones and rusted blades.
features.dm: Some of the dead don't stay down on the anniversary.

features.name: The burnt quarter
features.text: A quarter of {name} burned a generation ago and was never rebuilt; it is all blackened walls and weeds.
features.dm: The fire was set. The family who set it still lives in town.

features.name: The plague stones
features.text: Flat stones outside {name} mark where food was left for the town during a plague long ago.
features.dm: The plague came from somewhere. The records were burned.

features.name: The founding tree
features.text: An ancient tree in {name} is said to be where the first settlers camped.
features.dm: The tree is older than it looks, and it remembers.

features.name: The ruined tower
features.text: The stump of a wizard's tower stands on a hill above {name}, its top long since fallen.
features.dm: Its lower floors are intact, sealed, and the town has forgotten the way in.

features.name: The drowned church
features.text: When the river is low, the bell tower of a drowned church shows above the water at {name}.
features.dm: The church was drowned on purpose, to hide what was buried under it.

features.name: The hero's grave
features.text: A local hero is buried under a cairn in {name}; travellers leave small offerings.
features.dm: The grave is empty.

features.name: The old border stone
features.text: A carved stone in {name} marks a border between realms that no longer exist.
features.dm: Someone has been rubbing the inscription for a claim to the land.

features.name: The monster skull
features.text: The huge skull of a monster killed by the founders hangs over the gate of {name}.
features.dm: It was not killed. It was driven off, and its kind is long-lived.

features.name: The treaty hall
features.text: A small hall in {name} is where an old peace was signed, and the table is still kept.
features.dm: A copy of the treaty in the hall differs from the one in the city archives.

features.name: The outworlder's house
features.text: An outworlder lived in {name} long ago and built a house unlike any other, still standing.
features.dm: The house has a room the outworlder never showed anyone. It is still locked.

features.name: The flood marks
features.text: Marks on the wall of the old hall of {name} show how high every great flood has come.
features.dm: The marks are getting higher, faster.

controlPoints.name: {town} Outpost
controlPoints.text: A walled outpost on the road beyond {town}: a dozen soldiers, a signal fire and a stable.
controlPoints.yields: Control of the road, and tolls
controlPoints.dm: Whoever holds it sees everyone who comes and goes.

controlPoints.name: {town} Watchtower
controlPoints.text: A stone watchtower on the high ground above {town}, with a view for miles.
controlPoints.yields: Warning of anything coming, and a place to hold
controlPoints.dm: The old garrison left a cache under the floor.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Toll Fort
controlPoints.text: A small fort where the road crosses the river near {town}, taking a coin from every cart.
controlPoints.yields: Tolls, and a hand on trade
controlPoints.dm: The tolls go somewhere other than the books say.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Quarry
controlPoints.text: A quarry cut into the hills near {town}, its stone in every wall for miles.
controlPoints.yields: Stone for building, and work for the town
controlPoints.dm: A deep cut broke into an old cave last year, and it was quietly sealed.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Mine
controlPoints.text: An iron mine near {town}, its shafts lit day and night.
controlPoints.dm: The miners say a seam sings at night.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Crystal Workings
controlPoints.text: A mine near {town} where mana crystals grow in the rock, cut by careful hands and shipped under guard.
controlPoints.yields: Mana crystals, worth a fortune to mages and crafters
controlPoints.dm: Cutting too fast makes the crystals go wild, and someone wants it done fast.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Core Works
controlPoints.text: A refinery near {town} that renders monster cores into something crafters can use, stinking of ozone.
controlPoints.yields: Refined cores for crafting and ritual magic
controlPoints.dm: Some of the cores it buys come from monsters no one hunted.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Chalk Pits
controlPoints.text: White pits near {town} where ritual chalk is dug, every scrap of it sold to ritualists.
controlPoints.dm: Chalk from the deepest pit is stronger, and it is running out.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Lumber Camp
controlPoints.text: A logging camp in the woods near {town}, floating timber down the river.
controlPoints.dm: The loggers have cut into woods something else thinks of as its own.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Granary
controlPoints.text: The great granary of {town}, holding the harvest for the whole district.
controlPoints.yields: Grain, and the power to feed or starve a district
controlPoints.dm: The count in the books and the count in the bins do not match.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Bonded Warehouse
controlPoints.text: A guarded warehouse in {town} where merchants store goods before they are taxed.
controlPoints.yields: Goods, and a say in what moves through town
controlPoints.dm: A back room holds goods no one has declared.

controlPoints.name: The {town} Gate Camp
controlPoints.text: A fortified camp near {town} around an astral space entrance, with the Society's licence to work it.
controlPoints.yields: Loot and cores from the astral space
controlPoints.dm: The licence was bought, not earned.

details: Children's drawings cover every wall of the common room.
Bunks three high, and a waiting list.
A vegetable garden the children run themselves.
The roof leaks, and the buckets have names.
Lessons in the morning, chores in the afternoon.
Older children mind the younger ones.
Every child has a job, and a badge to show it.
A big dog guards the door and lets no strangers in.
Supper is the same stew every night, and everyone loves it.
The children put on a play every festival.
A tree in the yard has every child's name carved in it.
The building is a former noble's townhouse, too grand and too cold.
Lessons include reading, sums and how to spot a monster.
The children sleep in hammocks, like sailors.
The matron sings them all to sleep.
Visitors must bring a gift, even a small one.
The oldest children work at the docks and bring their wages home.
A chalkboard lists who was adopted and where they went.
There's a shrine to every god, so no child feels left out.
The children keep chickens and sell the eggs.
The front room doubles as a schoolroom for the neighbourhood.
A retired adventurer teaches sword drills on the green.
The building leans, and the children call it the Drunken House.
A brass bell calls them in from the streets at dusk.
The attic is full of toys donated over a hundred years.
The cook is a goblin who used to cook for a duke.
Every child gets a birthday, even those who don't know theirs, chosen on arrival.
The windows are barred, for reasons nobody explains.
The children have their own court and judge each other's quarrels.
A mural of famous adventurers covers the outside wall.
troubles: The money from the council has stopped coming.
Children have been going missing at night, one at a time.
A noble family claims one of the children as an heir.
The building is to be sold to a merchant who wants the land.
A sickness is going through the dormitory.
One child found an essence and is hiding it, desperate to use it before they're grown.
A gang is recruiting the older children as runners.
The matron has fallen ill and there's no one to replace her.
Food is short and the children are stealing.
A rich couple wants to adopt one child and separate them from a sibling.
The building has been condemned by the city.
A child has run away to join an adventuring team.
Someone keeps leaving money on the doorstep, and the matron wants to know who.
An older child is accused of a theft they didn't do.
A monster has been seen in the alley behind the building.
The church that runs it wants to send the children to work on its farms.
Two children are fighting over the same essence they found.
A father has come back for a child he left years ago.
The orphanage owes money to a moneylender who won't wait.
A child claims they're the heir of a noble house, and the house wants them quiet.
The neighbours complain about the noise and want the orphanage moved.
A fire damaged the kitchen, and there's nowhere to cook.
Several children have started sleepwalking to the same place.
A visiting priest is taking an unhealthy interest in one child.
The children's savings box has been stolen.
A recruiter from the steppe clans wants to take the older boys as riders.
The roof is about to fall in.
A child has a divine essence, granted early, and the church wants them.
A cold has turned into something worse.
The Adventure Society wants to use the building as a hall.
secrets: The matron sells the oldest children's names to a recruiter.
One of the children is an outworlder, and doesn't know it.
A cult pays the orphanage to send it 'apprentices'.
The founder's will left the building to the children, and someone hid it.
Two of the children are a famous adventurer's, left there in secret.
The building has a hidden room where a previous matron hid a fortune.
One child is a doppelganger that replaced a real child months ago.
The orphanage launders money for a crime boss.
The founder was a cultist, and the cult still visits on her birthday.
A child here is the real heir to the duke's title.
The children have found a way into the old tunnels and have been exploring.
The matron is a former assassin in hiding.
Children adopted from here are being sold to the Storm Kingdom.
The building sits on an astral space that hums at night.
A child's 'imaginary friend' is an astral being.
The council's inspector takes bribes to look the other way about the conditions.
The cook is poisoning the matron slowly, for reasons of her own.
An adventurer who grew up here is secretly paying all its bills.
Records of the children's parents are kept in a locked chest, and some are false.
A noble house uses the orphanage to hide its illegitimate children.
The orphanage's priest has lost the god's favour and fakes the blessings.
One of the children has a gift for seeing the future, and the matron is afraid of her.
The building was a prison once, and some cells are still in use.
A child has been writing to a god and getting answers.
The founders' ghosts still watch over the children.
